findings.reason: Confirmed (high). RS-05's VS4 keeps (research/blueprint/restructure/RS-05.result.json) and its Markdown row (RS-05.md, VS4 row of the retained-layer table) give VS4 'compact generation of Bun_G with compact objects of finite HN support and perfect compact-open invariants'. That mixes two different theorems of Fargues-Scholze (https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/Geometrization.pdf, read 2026-10-01). Theorem V.4.1 (p. 177): A is compact if and only if every i_b^*A is compact in D(G_b(E), Lambda) and zero for almost all b, where compactness means lying in the thick subcategory generated by c-Ind_K Lambda, K open pro-p. Theorem V.7.1 (p. 183): A is universally locally acyclic if and only if every M_b^K is a perfect complex. Propositions VII.7.4 (p. 273) and VII.7.9 (p. 275) make the same split for D_lis. The counterexample is right. Take E = Q_5, G = GL_1, H = Q_5^x, K = 1 + 5Z_5 and Lambda = F_3. V = c-Ind_K^H Lambda is one of V.4.1's own generators, so it is compact; on the degree-0 stratum (open and closed, since B(GL_1) = Z) it gives a compact, finitely supported object. H is abelian, so V^K = V = F_3[H/K] with H/K = Z x F_5^x, which is infinite-dimensional; K is pro-5 and 3 is invertible, so RGamma(K, V) = V[0] is not perfect. The atlas's own VS4 stage ('compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and ... the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups') and the packet node VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS4/compact-generation-and-compact-objects state V.4.1 correctly, and VS5/ula-equals-admissibility states V.7.1, so only RS-05 is wrong. The fix is right: in both RS-05 files, replace the clause by compact objects with compact stratum restrictions, zero on all but finitely many strata (equivalently the thick closure of the pro-p compact inductions); leave perfect derived K-invariants as VS5's ULA criterion; change neither the VS4 node nor the SR.2 imports.
